decisions.question: Adopt the third-party hide-diffs plugin, or build our own?

options.label: Build our own
options.summary: A new plugin in this marketplace, written from scratch; claude-setup enables it. No dependency on a third party's releases.

options.label: Adopt hide-diffs
options.summary: claude-setup enables hide-diffs@gixxy22-plugins and writes its shortcuts. Small, but the standard depends on a plugin we do not control.

decisions.owner_words: build our own; create the new plugin so all of this is offered in one marketplace; DO NOT copy hidediffs code

decisions.question: How are the plugin's hooks tested?

options.label: Node test runner on pure logic
options.summary: All logic in plain .ts files with no Claude Code imports, tested by node --test (Node strips the types; no npm). The thin hooks file is checked by claude plugin validate and a smoke checklist.

options.label: claude-code/testing kit
options.summary: Tests run through claude plugin test against a fake engine; covers the drawing code too, but ties the tests to Claude Code's early-access kit.

decisions.chosen: Node test runner on pure logic
decisions.owner_words: why do you need claude-code/testing? if possible avoid it

decisions.question: Which single marketplace name should the repo, README and installs use?

options.label: dev-standards
options.summary: Rename marketplace.json's name to match the repo and what this machine already registered; README says @dev-standards everywhere.

options.label: luismc-dev-tools
options.summary: Keep the manifest name; re-register the marketplace on this machine and re-enable the plugins.

decisions.question: What is the new plugin called?

options.label: luismc-transcript-folds
options.summary: Folder claude/plugins/transcript-folds; names exactly what it does.

options.label: luismc-transcript
options.summary: Folder claude/plugins/transcript; shorter but more generic.

options.label: luismc-diff-summary
options.summary: Folder claude/plugins/diff-summary; says diffs only, though it also folds commands.

decisions.question: Which shortcuts toggle diffs and folded commands?

options.label: ctrl+x d / ctrl+x f
options.summary: Chords in Claude Code's own ctrl+x family, both free, on every terminal and OS; slash commands as a fallback. Unlike ctrl+q (flow control) and alt+q (Option on macOS).

options.label: ctrl+x h / ctrl+x c
options.summary: Same family: h for hide diffs, c for commands. Also free.

options.label: Slash commands only
options.summary: No keybindings.json changes; toggle with two slash commands.

decisions.owner_words: recommend other keyboard shorts different from the ones in hide-diff

decisions.question: Does the first version include all four parts: hidden diffs, folded commands, the session tally and compact mode?

options.label: Yes
options.summary: Hide long diffs, fold shell commands, a session tally above the prompt and a compact-mode setting.

options.label: No
options.summary: A smaller first version with some of them left out.

decisions.question: How does claude-setup offer the new plugin?

options.label: Standard, user target
options.summary: Always applied: enables the plugin in ~/.claude/settings.json and adds the two chords to ~/.claude/keybindings.json, asking only on a chord conflict.

options.label: Asked each run
options.summary: A step-1 yes/no question; the same writes on yes.

options.label: Standard, project target
options.summary: Enabled per project in .claude/settings.json; keybindings still go to ~/.claude.

decisions.question: What state does a fresh install start in?

options.label: Diffs hidden, commands folded
options.summary: Both switches on; the choice is remembered across sessions afterwards.

options.label: Diffs hidden, commands shown
options.summary: Only diffs fold by default.

options.label: Both off
options.summary: Nothing changes until a shortcut is pressed.

decisions.question: Does DS63 (the clarifying-questions rule) ride the same release as this feature?

options.label: One train
options.summary: DS63, the marketplace rename and this plugin with its claude-setup change: one fold, one ready PR, one CI run, one merge.

options.label: DS63 first
options.summary: Release DS63 alone now; this feature follows on a second train.

decisions.question: What happens to hide-diffs on the owner's machine once this plugin is live?

options.label: Owner uninstalls it
options.summary: The owner removes it with one command; until then both coexist with different shortcuts and actions.

options.label: Keep both
options.summary: No shared shortcuts, but both redraw the same tool rows; whichever loads last wins.
